newsitem.title: CHINA: HONG KONG GOLD CLOSES AT DAY'S LOW ON LATE SELLING.
newsitem.headline: HONG KONG GOLD CLOSES AT DAY'S LOW ON LATE SELLING.

text.p: Gold was dumped in Hong Kong on Tuesday, extending early losses to close at the day's low on late selling, after rises in New York overnight, dealers said.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$327.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$328.20/70 close on Monday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$326.20/70.

"Morning trade kicked off with light sales from Japanese traders due to the yen's depreciation," said a dealer at a local investment house. "But as the market waited, no buying emerged and the sellers are coming back in late trade."
"The sentiment was still on the cautious side of bearish," another dealer said. "Support was generally seen at around $320 to $322 levels and resistance at US$330."
Local gold ended HK$8 higher at HK$3,026 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.50 from its previous fix at -7.00.
